answer: The founder casts his mark into every bell and records its tone in the mould book when the bell is rung for the first time. A mirror bell bought from another foundry fails the book: at the saffron of the tone the note must match the founder's own record, and a strange bell rings differently. Forging a bell means building a furnace, casting forty bells and paying 31,500 in bronze and fuel, while the signal mark in the bronze is checked at every church, so a bell whose tone was never measured is melted down.
